Thoughts on keto.

Hi v/keto! I've been doing low-carb/keto for about 4 years and below are some thoughts on the subject. These are my own opinions and experiences and I don't claim they are true or work for anyone but myself. I am also not a naive English speaker

Obesity is a hormonal disorder and total calories don't matter that much

When we eat large amounts of processed carbohydrates and vegetable oils, our hormone system gets damaged. The process typically takes decades, but in later years even young people are subjects. When we eat carbohydrates, the hormone insulin is secreted. The purpose of insulin is to stimulate cells to absorb the glucose that is produced when we eat carbohydrates. This is vital because our body gets damaged by high glucose levels in the blood. If we eat moderate amounts of carbohydrates everything works, but if we eat too much we can develop insulin insensitivity also known as pre diabetes. The cells can only absorb a certain amount of carbohydrates and if the blood sugar stays high, the insulin stays high. This in turn starts another process where the body promotes fat cell growth and the liver starts converting carbohydrates into fat that is stored in those cells.

To produce all kinds of hormones the body needs cholesterol. Cholesterol is produced by the liver and it needs dietary fat to do it. But the fat needs to be of good quality. Processed vegetable oil is not good quality in this case and if that is our main source of fat, the amounts of cholesterol and thus hormones the body can produce will be limited and it will prioritize insulin because if blood sugar is not taken care of, we die. Cortisol is another hormone with high priority that is produced when we sleep to little and live stressful lives. Cortisol also promotes weight gain.

Hormone or Endocrine disruptors is a hot subject today, and ironically, the most endocrine disrupting substances are on most peoples table every day - processed carbohydrates and vegetable fats. If consumed in excessive amounts that is. Which todays dietary guidelines advice us to do.

Because of this, almost everyone have an hormonal disorder today which can lead to weight gain and more serious problems like cardiovascular disease, cancer, dementia, et al. I will not go into the processes behind this here, but if you want to read about the, in my opinion, best hypotheses on cancer google Thomas Seyfreid.

So how do we fix our hormonal disorder?

As I said, the process typically takes decades, and it can take years to repair the damage. Here are some advice:

  • Eat keto. But stay clear from processed foods. Some carbs can be ok, but maybe not if you're primarily aiming for weight loss. High quality fats are important. Look into Paleo.

  • Do cardio in the morning a few days per week on an empty stomach and don't eat until lunch. This promotes production of the types of hormones that are suppressed. For example sex hormones. These hormones promote weight loss and overall health.

  • Control what you eat and when you eat (few meals), but eat until you are full when you eat. Otherwise you risk down rating your metabolism.

  • Sleep and remove stress from your life.

  • Get lots of sunlight. Moderate sun bathing does not promote skin cancer. It's again processed carbohydrates and vegetable oils that does that. The sun gives us vitamin D which is another vital hormone.

Those are my cents. Keto on brothers and sisters!

If you're a fan of Dan Carlin there are also several other great History focused podcasts out there. A few of my personal favorites are

The History of Rome by Mike Duncan - 179 glorious episodes that detail the very beginnings of the original Rome as founded by Romulus all the way through the fall of the Western Empire in the 400's AD. It was wrapped up in 2012 I believe but still very much worthy of a listen.

The History of Byzantium by Robin Pierson - A continuation of the original The History of Rome podcast that follows the Eastern Empire from 476 AD to 1453 when Constaninople fell. Updates once every two weeks or so and a great continuation from what I have listened to so far.

Revolutions by Mike Duncan - Mike Duncan's followup to his The History of Rome podcast in which he closely examines several Revolutions throughout history.
